findings.reason: naming these owners lets the author extend them (make `structure_templates` pattern-keyed; reuse or retire `concepts.yaml`) instead of shipping a third parallel vocabulary, and the plan's "what none of them hold" claim is only true if it has read them.
findings.text: the prior-art search is incomplete: §2 proposes `templates.yml` holding "one description opening and one documentation opening per name pattern, the section order, and the sign-convention rule", but the repo already ships that guidance under `entry_schema.fields.documentation.guidance` (`structure_templates.opening_paragraph` at specification.yml:587-606, `equations.symbols` at :639, `sign_conventions` at :659-668), code-generated into `imas_standard_names/grammar/field_schemas.py:57` and served to consumers; and §2 proposes `notation.yml`/`concepts.yml` without citing `imas_codex/definitions/clusters/concepts.yaml`, the consumer's existing physics-concept vocabulary that already carries `symbol:` and `units:` annotations per concept (concepts.yaml:26-41; `symbol: Te` at concepts.yaml:30). Neither is named in §1 or §2.

findings.reason: the plan should add the equation/symbol fields to the existing `vocab_loaders.py` entry models and key off those, or state explicitly how the two definitions reconcile; a second definition string per token drifts.
findings.text: `concepts.yml` carries "a one-sentence definition" keyed by the operator, locus, coordinate or base token, which is a second owner of definitions that three existing vocabulary entries already hold and the codebase already exposes: `LocusEntry.definition` (vocab_loaders.py:81, 187 entries in `locus_registry.yml`), `PhysicalBaseDef.definition` (vocab_loaders.py:194, 24 entries in `physical_bases.yml`), `GeometryCarrierDef.definition` (vocab_loaders.py:231), consumed by `imas_standard_names/grammar/terms.py:29` and `:41` and `imas_standard_names/grammar/context.py:908`. The ISN plan §2 omits the caveat its imas-codex sibling `sn-house-style` §2 carries ("Where ISN already defines a token … the entry builds on that definition rather than restating it"), so as written the definition is restated.

findings.reason: a forbidden-spelling registry that does not name the existing `aliases`/`abbreviations` owners will let a token be forbidden in one place and aliased in another, with no gate to catch it.
findings.text: `notation.yml` ("one symbol per quantity or coordinate … keyed by base, subject, component or coordinate token, with its forbidden spellings") is a second owner of alternate spellings already held at `LocusEntry.abbreviations` (vocab_loaders.py:83), `PhysicalBaseDef.aliases` (vocab_loaders.py:189) and `GeometryCarrierDef.aliases` (vocab_loaders.py:229), and of symbols already held per quantity at `imas_standard_names/resources/tokamak_parameters/jet.yml:18` (`symbol: R_0`) and imas-codex `imas_codex/definitions/clusters/concepts.yaml:30` (`symbol: Te`).

findings.reason: extending `vocab_loaders.py` with the new entries and adding the parse-selection function to `terms.py` reuses the existing refusal and accessor instead of adding a third loader module beside two.
findings.text: the plan adds "a pydantic model and a loader" plus "a public accessor [that] takes a parsed name and returns exactly the entries that apply", a second owner of machinery that already exists twice here: `grammar/loader.py:108` `load_advisory_aliases` is a keyed-by-segment registry loader that refuses unknown segment keys (loader.py:120-144), and `grammar/vocab_loaders.py:546` `validate_no_cross_registry_duplicates` already owns "refuse a key that is not a real token"; `grammar/terms.py:22,49,63` (`standard_terms`/`fetch_standard_terms`/`search_standard_terms`) already owns the governed-token→definition accessor.

findings.reason: the honest change is to key `structure_templates` by pattern family in `specification.yml` (one owner, regenerated into `field_schemas.py`), not to fork a second template source that the two will drift between.
findings.text: `templates.yml` is a thin layer over existing machinery: `entry_schema.fields.documentation.guidance.structure_templates` already holds the opening template (specification.yml:588-591 → field_schemas.py:58) and the section order (specification.yml:592-598 → field_schemas.py:63), and `sign_conventions` holds the sign-convention rule (specification.yml:659-668); the plan adds a parallel file rather than making that guidance pattern-keyed, and does not say why the existing guidance cannot be extended.

findings.reason: the section must account for the public surface it adds against the supplied counts; here it can name the retirement concretely — the accessor and refusal reuse `terms.py`/`vocab_loaders.py` and the `templates.yml` content merges into `specification.yml` — so the accounting is available and simply absent.
findings.text: public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 adds a public accessor, a pydantic model and loader, and a new refusal family (the loader "refuses any key that is not a real token in the current vocabularies", per file, by name), without naming in its own text what it retires or merges, or stating why nothing can be.

response_events.reason: per-pattern openings are data selected from a name's parse, while specification.yml documentation guidance is the generic writer rubric generated into field_schemas.py and carried by every entry's schema, so keying it by pattern would put per-pattern data into a schema every consumer loads; templates.yml now references the section order and the generic sign-convention form in specification.yml rather than restating them, so the two sources cannot drift

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the single accessor hides the three files, the three key-spaces (token kind, quantity kind, pattern family) and the selection behind one call, so the complexity sits behind an interface smaller than what it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `concepts.yml` and `notation.yml` are a second owner of per-token definitions and alternate spellings already held in `grammar/vocab_loaders.py`, and the loader/accessor are a second owner of machinery in `grammar/loader.py` and `grammar/terms.py`; the finding names each site below.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 adds a public accessor, a loader and a token-key refusal family without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites `docs/guidelines.md`, the locus registry and the shipped symbol-definition policy, but does not cite two of the three owners its new files would duplicate: `imas_standard_names/grammar/specification.yml` `entry_schema` documentation guidance and imas-codex `imas_codex/definitions/clusters/concepts.yaml`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — `templates.yml` re-adds the documentation opening, section order and sign-convention rule that `specification.yml` already generates, and the plan says nothing about extending that mechanism to be pattern-keyed.
